one_month_reasoning: No CoreWeave earnings in the window (Q3 report expected ~Nov 9-16, outside Oct 31). In-window events: hyperscaler earnings Oct 27 (MSFT, GOOGL), Oct 28 (META), Oct 29 (AMZN) whose 2027 capex guides and Microsoft's commentary (CoreWeave's largest customer) typically move neoclouds 5-15%; FOMC Oct 28 with Polymarket at 75% hold / 25% +25bp hike (~$22M volume) against a 10y at 5.29%, a headwind for a ~$44B-debt name; continued ATM selling (up to 35M shares) is a mild drag. The stock has rebounded from $78 to $88.57 after the Sept 17 dilution drop, with no strong momentum signal. I stay near neutral: lognormal centred slightly below spot ($86.8, reflecting ATM supply and the lognormal median-below-mean effect) with sigma 0.28 for the month (93%/3.5 = 0.27, nudged up for the hyperscaler/FOMC cluster).

fair_value.method: Blend of a DCF ($35/sh: WACC 11%, revenue $24.5B in 2027 to $64B in 2032, 60-62% EBITDA margin, 2.5-3.0x capex intensity, 6-yr GPU life, g 3%, end-2027 net debt $72B, 610M shares) at 40% weight and 6.0x EV/NTM EBITDA on ~$20B Oct-2027 NTM EBITDA ($79/sh) at 60%; = ~$61. The DCF is extremely sensitive (WACC 10-12% gives $57-$17; capex intensity 2.25-2.75x gives $68-$2) because the equity is a thin slice above a large, debt-funded EV.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Unlevered FCF 2028-32 of -$5.6B, $8.0B, $12.4B, $16.8B, $11.9B; terminal FCF $8.7B (60% EBITDA margin less 2.5x/6 replacement capex x0.85, 21% tax, growth capex 2.5x g) capitalised at 11%-3% = TV $109B; EV at end-2027 $93B less net debt $72B = $21B / 610M shares = $35.

inputs_detail.derivation: Midpoint of raised guide $12.4-13.2B; matches 40-analyst consensus $12.87B.

Exit-2026 annualized run-rate $18.5-19.5B (mgmt) plus active power going from >1.85 GW (end-2026 guide) toward >3 GW by end-2027 (target discussed on call) at ~$10M revenue per active MW (=$19B ARR / 1.85 GW); averaged through the year.

Contracted power 4.2 GW and ~6 GW incl. powered land vs. >=8 GW 2030 target; backlog $104B + $25B Q3 commitments. I assume ~6-6.5 GW productive by 2030 at ~$9M/MW (older-vintage price decay) i.e. a haircut to the 8 GW goal for power/moratorium delays flagged on the call and the asset-growth base rate that hyper-growth asset builders under-deliver vs extrapolation.

Q2-26 adj. EBITDA margin 59%; mgmt says new contracts carry 5-10pp higher contribution margin and margins expand sequentially; terminal trimmed to 60% for renewal repricing risk on second contracts (Cape Fear).
2026 capex guide $35-39B (mid $37B) funds roughly $11.7B of 2027 revenue added -> ~3.2x; assumed to fall to 2.5x as newer SKUs price higher (mgmt: Blackwell/Vera Rubin pricing at new highs).

inputs_detail.value: 6-year life; fleet replaced at 85% of original cost
inputs_detail.derivation: CoreWeave depreciates GPUs straight-line over 6 years with zero salvage; replacement at 85% of original cost assumes some cost-per-compute deflation.

inputs_detail.value: 0% through 2029 (NOLs, valuation allowance), 21% on EBIT after
inputs_detail.derivation: Company records a valuation allowance on net DTAs and is loss-making; US statutory 21% thereafter.
Rf 5.29% + 2.0 x 5% ERP; beta of ~2 judged from 93% realized vol (brief) and price history showing multiple 40-60% drawdowns since IPO.
Q3 interest guide $860-940M (annualized ~$3.6B) on ~$35-40B debt (Jun-30 total debt $35.1B plus new issuance).
~52% equity ($48B market cap) at 15.3% + ~48% debt (~$44B gross incl. new converts) at 7.1% = 11.4%, rounded to 11% to credit contracted/IG-customer cash flows.
Roughly nominal GDP; below Rf 5.29%. Note: with ROIC near WACC, higher g barely helps (g=4% lowers value) because growth capex absorbs the cash.

Jun-26 debt $35.1B less cash $5.5B = $29.6B; H2-26 burn ~$20B (EBITDA ~$4.9B less ~$23B capex less ~$1.9B interest) less ~$3B ATM equity -> ~$47B end-2026; 2027 EBITDA $14.7B less ~$35B capex less ~$4.5B interest -> +$25B.
Q2 diluted weighted 551M + up to 35M ATM shares + ~2%/yr SBC and convert dilution.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 6.0x x $20B NTM EBITDA = $120B EV less $72B net debt = $48B / 610M shares = $79.

inputs_detail.derivation: Between modelled 2027 EBITDA $14.7B (=$24.5B x 60%) and 2028 $22B, weighted to 2028; built on Q2 59% margin and run-rate guidance.

Today's EV ~ $48B mkt cap + $35.1B debt + $3B converts - $5.5B cash = ~$80.6B over ~$13.5B NTM EBITDA (exit ARR $19B x ~60% margin, ramping) = ~6x; held flat because neocloud peers are de-rating on capex/financing worries rather than re-rating.

bear.story: AI-capex digestion or a hyperscaler pull-back (Polymarket ~20% on an 'AI bubble burst' by end-2026) meets 5%+ long rates: new contract pricing rolls over, Vera Rubin deliveries slip on power/moratoria, and the market prices the equity on the DCF reality that cash after replacement capex barely covers debt; more ATM/convert dilution. EV/EBITDA compresses to ~4.5-5x on 2028 EBITDA.

base.story: Execution roughly on plan (2027 revenue ~$24-26B, >3 GW active, adj. op margin low-teens) but the stock keeps trading as a levered AI-sentiment instrument at ~6x forward EBITDA with net debt rising ~$25B a year and ongoing dilution, so price ends a little below today despite strong revenue growth; consistent with the asset-growth base rate of sub-par returns for the highest-asset-growth decile.

bull.story: Backlog keeps compounding ($104B + $25B already), pricing on Blackwell/Vera Rubin holds at record levels, credit profile moves toward investment grade cutting interest costs, rates ease, and the multiple re-rates toward 8x as 2028 EBITDA visibility (> $22B) firms; stock revisits the $150s seen in Oct 2025 and in analyst targets (avg $141.58).

thesis_break_reason: $45 is ~25% below the 52-week low ($60.55, set July 2026) and implies EV/2027 EBITDA near 4x, i.e. the market pricing credit stress: a failed or very expensive refinancing, a major customer (Microsoft/OpenAI-type) cancelling or deferring capacity, or evidence that second-contract renewal pricing collapses. At that level my base case (equity holds ~6x on a growing EBITDA base) is wrong rather than merely volatile.

key_uncertainties: Capital intensity and renewal pricing of GPU fleets: DCF value swings from ~$0 to ~$70/sh on +/-0.25x capex intensity or 5pp terminal margin.
Funding: net debt likely rises from ~$30B to ~$70B+ by end-2027 while long rates sit at 5.3%; refinancing/dilution terms drive equity value.
Customer concentration (Microsoft ~40% of H1-26 revenue) and hyperscaler capex cycle.
Power delivery and local data-center moratoria affecting the 3 GW (2027) / 8 GW (2030) ramp.
Sentiment regime for AI infrastructure; stock has round-tripped $40 -> $187 -> $64 -> $153 -> $61 -> $88 since IPO.
reasoning: Facts: Q2-26 revenue $2.58B (+112%), adj. EBITDA 59%, net loss $626M, debt $35.1B vs cash $5.5B; FY26 guide revenue $12.4-13.2B, capex $35-39B, exit ARR $18.5-19.5B; backlog $104B + $25B; contracted 4.2 GW. Sept 17 ATM (35M sh) + $3B converts. Valuation: an explicit DCF (WACC 11% off a 5.29% 10y, 6-yr GPU life, 2.5-3x capex intensity, 60-62% margins) gives only ~$35 because replacement and growth capex absorb most EBITDA and net debt reaches ~$72B by end-2027; a market-multiple method (today's ~6x EV/NTM EBITDA rolled forward) gives ~$79. Blended fair value ~$61, below the $88.57 price and far below sell-side ($141.58 avg), which I treat as optimistic evidence. Base rates: (1) CRWV's own history is violently mean-reverting inside a $60-155 band for the past year, with 93% realized vol, so a random-walk sigma (~0.85) overstates dispersion slightly; I use an effective log-sd ~0.66 with a fat left tail. (2) Highest-asset-growth firms historically underperform by ~10%/yr risk-adjusted (Cooper-Gulen-Schill), and CoreWeave is an extreme case. (3) Prediction markets give ~20% to an AI-bubble burst by end-2026 and a 25% chance the Fed hikes in October, a hostile rate backdrop for a leveraged long-duration asset. (4) Peers (Nebius, IREN) are de-rating on capex/financing, not demand. I therefore set a median ~$81 (modestly below spot, pulled toward fair value but not converging within a year given momentum and backlog), mean ~$96 (right tail from AI-demand upside), via a 27/48/25 mixture of lognormals centred at $38/$82/$155. P(>= $89) ~44%, P(>= $53) ~74%, P(>= $155) ~15%. Research limits: Twelve Data fundamentals/estimates and Alpha Vantage were paywalled/rate-limited; 2027 consensus figures were not verifiable, so 2027 revenue is derived from management run-rate guidance.
